issue.title: Push notifications only work when app is open
issue.body:
### Description

After updating to the latest version (v2026.5.22+25), push notifications are only delivered when the app is actively open/foregrounded. When the app is in the background or closed, no push notifications are received.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Receive a new DM/group message while the app is open → ✅ notification received
2. Close the app or send it to the background
3. Receive a new message → ❌ no notification delivered

### Expected Behavior

Push notifications should be delivered even when the app is in the background or terminated, as per standard platform push notification behavior (APNs on iOS, FCM on Android).

### Environment

- App version: v2026.5.22+25
- Platform: iOS
- OS version: 26.5

### Additional Context

This was tested with MLS-encrypted DMs via a marmot protocol relay. Messages are delivered correctly when the app is open; the issue is specifically with background/terminated-state push delivery.

Release notes

Sourced from flutter_secure_storage's releases.

v10.3.0

Android

  • Added AndroidBiometricType enum and biometricType option to AndroidOptions to control which authentication methods are accepted during biometric prompts (requires KeyCipherAlgorithm.AES_GCM_NoPadding).
    • AndroidBiometricType.biometricOrDeviceCredential (default) accepts Class 3 biometrics or device credentials (PIN/pattern/password), preserving previous behaviour.
    • AndroidBiometricType.strongBiometricOnly restricts authentication to Class 3 (strong) biometrics only; device credentials are explicitly rejected.
  • Fully enforced on Android 11+ (API 30+) via setAllowedAuthenticators on BiometricPrompt and setUserAuthenticationParameters on the KeyStore key. On earlier API levels the system may still permit device credentials.
  • Added biometricPromptNegativeButton option to AndroidOptions to customise the dismiss button label on the biometric prompt. Required when using strongBiometricOnly or on Android 10 and lower.

iOS / macOS

  • Fixed secStoreAvailabilitySink not being called when protected data availability changes.
  • Fixed kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain being added to Keychain queries unconditionally; it is now only set when useDataProtectionKeychain is explicitly enabled.

Windows

  • Fixed deleteAll and containsKey not acquiring the mutex lock, which could cause data races under concurrent access. If you are on Dart >=3.10.0, this fix is applied automatically. Otherwise, pin flutter_secure_storage_windows: ^4.2.2 in your pubspec.yaml to opt in and make sure your constraint is set for minimum of Dart >=3.10.0.

Linux

  • Fixed deleteKeyring storing the string "null" instead of an empty JSON object {}.
  • Fixed non-UTF-8 error messages from libsecret causing a FormatException on the Dart side; messages are now sanitised before being sent through the method channel.
  • Fixed locked or unavailable keyring now surfacing as a catchable PlatformException with code KeyringLocked.
  • Fixed JSON parse errors and other C++ exceptions now surfacing as a PlatformException with code StorageError instead of sending malformed bytes through the channel.

issue.title: Notification permission UX: in-app explainer before system prompt
issue.body:
## Context
From PR #262 review — currently `requestPermission()` fires immediately on first login with no user context. On Android 13+, if the user denies, the system remembers the denial.

## Description
Add an in-app explanation screen/dialog before requesting the system notification permission. This should:
- Explain why notifications are needed (to receive messages when the app is backgrounded)
- Show before the first system permission prompt
- Not re-show if the user has already granted/denied
- Respect the notification account settings (#267)

## Additional UX
- The battery optimization exemption request (`REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`) also needs user-facing explanation, since it triggers a system dialog
- Consider combining both into a single onboarding flow after first login

## Related
- PR #262 (local notifications)
- #265 (notification message improvements)
- #267 (notification navigation)

review.body:
I tried it and it works fine for me 👍🏻  but my agent left a review with request changes conclusions. We are about to get in the plane soon so I'm not able to review it more deeply but I leave the comments of my agent and let you decide if there are hallucinations or not:

>🤖  ### 🔴 must — block ship until fixed
> 
> **M1. `ui.Image` returned by `toImageSync` is never disposed — native-memory leak per long-press attempt.** `lib/screens/share_profile_screen.dart:81-83`
> ```dart
> final captureFuture = boundary
>     .toImageSync(pixelRatio: 3)
>     .toByteData(format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png);
> ```
> Per Flutter docs (`RenderRepaintBoundary.toImageSync`): *"The returned image must be disposed by the caller, see Image.dispose."* The intermediate `ui.Image` here is anonymous, so nothing ever calls `dispose()` on it. At `pixelRatio: 3` on a 256-logical-pixel square, each capture allocates ~2.4 MB of Skia-owned native memory. In debug mode this fires Flutter's `Image.dispose()` warning the first time the user long-presses — and on iOS, repeated long-presses on a memory-constrained device can pressure the app group container (notification service extension shares memory budget).
> *How to address:*
> ```dart
> final image = boundary.toImageSync(pixelRatio: 3);
> try {
>   final byteData = await image.toByteData(format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png);
>   // ...use byteData...
> } finally {
>   image.dispose();
> }
> ```
> The `image.dispose()` must run on *every* exit path, including the existing early-return branches (`!isMounted.value`, `!isHolding.value`, `byteData == null`) and the `catch`.
> 
> **M2. Captured PNG includes the `ClipRRect`'s transparent corners — the shared image renders with transparent rounded corners.** `lib/screens/share_profile_screen.dart:191-217`
> The `RepaintBoundary(key: qrRepaintKey)` wraps `ConstrainedBox > AspectRatio > ClipRRect > AnimatedBuilder > QrImageView`. `toImageSync` captures the boundary's *rendered* output, which means the four rounded-corner regions are encoded as fully-transparent pixels in the PNG. When the recipient opens the file in (a) iMessage's dark-mode bubble, (b) any messenger that renders attachments on a non-white background, or (c) Gallery's dark theme, the QR will appear to have four small dark-blob corners.
> This is a real UX bug for the "I want my friend to scan this" use case — and worse, on some scanners the transparent corners are alpha-blended against an arbitrary background and the corner *finder patterns* of the QR (which intentionally sit near the corners) can come out with halos that hurt scan reliability.
> *How to address:* either capture from a wrapper widget that paints an opaque background behind the QR (move the `RepaintBoundary` *inside* the `ClipRRect`, or wrap the QR in a `Container(color: colors.backgroundSecondary)` before the boundary), or — preferably — drop the rounded clip for the captured image by capturing a separate non-clipped offstage widget. Add a golden test that asserts the four corners of the PNG are opaque.
> 
> **M3. `boundary == null` is a silent failure — the user is left holding the QR with no feedback.** `lib/screens/share_profile_screen.dart:71-75`
> ```dart
> final boundary = qrRepaintKey.currentContext?.findRenderObject() as RenderRepaintBoundary?;
> if (boundary == null) {
>   isCapturing.value = false;
>   return;
> }
> ```

No `showErrorNotice` is shown, no log is emitted. This *should* never happen in practice — but if a future refactor breaks the key wiring (e.g., wrapping the boundary in a conditional `Builder`), this branch becomes a guaranteed bug that's hard to diagnose because the failure is invisible.
> *How to address:* on `boundary == null`, call `showErrorNotice(context.l10n.shareQrCodeError)` and log at warning level. Add a unit test that fakes the `qrRepaintKey.currentContext` to null (or refactors capture into a hook so it can be tested in isolation) and asserts the error notice is shown.
> 
> **M4. `start_chat_screen_test.dart` invite-share test no longer asserts the file payload, only `.text` — coverage regression on the *only* other call site of `SharePlus.instance.share`.** `test/screens/start_chat_screen_test.dart:512-519`
> Diff trades a `MethodCall.arguments['text']` check for `shareCalls[0].text`. That's fine, but `ShareParams` also accepts `files: …`. If a future regression adds a stray `files: [XFile.fromData(…)]` to the invite-share call (copy-paste from the new QR share code), this test passes silently because it never asserts `shareCalls[0].files`.
> *How to address:* add `expect(shareCalls[0].files, isNull, reason: 'invite share is text-only')`. Cheap and prevents this exact category of cross-contamination since both share call sites now share the same fixture.

issue.title: fix(mentions): use accent Color/500 so mentions stay legible on both bubbles
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/12fc74d461a4b879e9a68324e78d2076bf39151b9536cf557f51dcd8ad1c79f6.png) Mentions disappear on the "wrong-side" bubble in each theme. In dark mode an orange username sits at orange-50 (near-white) on a white outgoing bubble. Vlad caught it and posted the spec. The mention renderer was reading `AvatarColorSet.content`, wired to `accent.contentPrimary`. That step is `Color/900` in light mode and `Color/50` in dark, so it inverts with the theme and clashes with whichever bubble is the opposite shade. That token belongs on the tinted avatar pill, not the chat bubble. Per the foundations file (node 297-1992), mentions should use `Accent/{color}/Content Secondary`, which is `Color/500` in both modes. The 500 step is mid-saturation and reads on both white and near-black bubbles. ### Changes - `lib/utils/avatar_color.dart`: add `contentSecondary` to `AvatarColorSet`. Wires to `accent.contentSecondary` for accent buckets and `fillContentTertiary` for the neutral bucket. - `lib/widgets/markdown_text.dart`: npub mention text uses `.contentSecondary`. - `test/widgets/markdown_text_test.dart`: widget test asserts the mention color equals `contentSecondary` and is not `content`. Regression guard so a future marmot does not revert it by accident. ### Scope Mentions only. Sender names and reply-author labels have the same root cause but are outside Vlad's note. The new field is in place if we apply the rule to them later. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Style** * Updated visual styling of mentions to use improved secondary color variants, providing better visual distinction and consistency across the interface. * **Tests** * Enhanced test coverage to verify mention color styling behavior. issue.title: Support Android in integration tests
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/dd1ac80777d20141b7bd33d3f22d917f040b45872cfbc5ca53d126f3f81f30ba.jpg) `just int-test` now runs on Android. ## What changed - `_resolve-device` falls back to `adb devices` when no booted iOS simulator is found, and skips `xcrun` on hosts where it isn't installed (so Linux works too). - `int-test` auto-injects public Nostr relays through `--dart-define=WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...` when the resolved device is an Android one. The emulator can't reach the host's localhost, so the local docker relays aren't usable there. - `integration_test/_support/app_setup.dart` reads the relay list from that dart-define (default: the same two localhost relays as before), and the TCP precheck now no-ops for non-localhost URLs. The iOS path is unchanged, and either platform can override the relay list with `WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...`. ## Why The marmot colony hibernates near the host, but our Android sibling lives one virtual network away (it can't hear the local relays burrowing at `127.0.0.1`). So when the Android marmot wants to chat, we point it at the public relays already used in production: `nos.lol`, `relay.primal.net`, `relay.damus.io`. ## How to use ```bash # iOS simulator (unchanged) just int-test # Android emulator (auto-detected, auto-uses public relays) just int-test # Override relays on any platform WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=wss://my.relay just int-test ``` --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Integration tests accept a comma-separated relay env var (trimmed, empty entries dropped) and pass it into test runs. * Local relay preflight parses each relay URL, validates only localhost/127.0.0.1 hosts for connectivity, and derives the port from the URL or scheme. * Device resolution now detects both booted iOS simulators and connected Android devices; test runs adapt accordingly. * **Chores** * Android test flow adds automatic port forwarding for Android devices when needed and enables debug build network config to allow cleartext to localhost. # Context
When clicking in a user tag in a message bubble, it shows the start chat screen. A solution that we discussed here https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/665#discussion_r3261928955 would be to keep the start chat navigation only for users that are not members of the group and for group members navigate to the group member screen
